post.summary: Creates an attendant by linking an existing User to a Location.
post.description: This endpoint creates an instance of the UserAttendant model, which represents an attendant assignment. It links an existing User (who has the ATTENDANT role) to a Location where they will work. Both the User and Location must already exist in the system. The UserAttendant model stores references to both the User and Location. This is an alias for the registerAttendant functionality. Use /createUser first to create the User with ATTENDANT role, then use this endpoint to assign them to a specific location.

idToken.description: Firebase authentication token of the administrator creating the attendant assignment. This token is used to verify the admin's identity and ensure they have permission to create attendant assignments. The token is obtained from Firebase Authentication after the admin logs in.

data.description: Payload containing search criteria to find the User and Location to link together.

user.description: Search criteria to find an existing User. You can provide any unique property like 'id' or 'email'. Keys must be valid properties of the User model. The first matching User will be used.

location.description: Search criteria to find an existing Location. You can provide any unique property like 'id' or 'name'. Keys must be valid properties of the Location model. The first matching Location will be used.

200.description: UserAttendant instance successfully created. The attendant has been assigned to the specified location.

attendant.description: The newly created UserAttendant instance. This object represents the assignment of an attendant (User) to a specific Location. It contains an auto-generated ID and references to both the User and Location documents.

id.description: Auto-generated unique identifier for this UserAttendant instance.

user.description: Reference to the User document representing the attendant.

id.description: The ID of the User document.

location.description: Reference to the Location document where the attendant is assigned.

id.description: The ID of the Location document.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this attendant assignment was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when this attendant assignment was last updated.

createdBy.description: Email of the administrator who created this assignment.

400.description: Bad Request - Missing required fields, Invalid search properties, User/Location not found, or relationship already exists.

error.description: Detailed error message explaining what went wrong.
examples: User criteria object is required to find the user.
Location criteria object is required to find the location.
Invalid search properties for User: invalidProp. Valid properties are: id, email, firstName...
Invalid search properties for Location: invalidProp. Valid properties are: id, name, address...
Location not found matching criteria: {"name":"Unknown Lot"}
Failed to create attendant relationship: Duplicate entry

401.description: Unauthorized - Missing or invalid authentication token.

403.description: Forbidden - Valid token but insufficient permissions.

500.description: Internal Server Error - Unexpected server-side error.

error.example: Internal Server Error: Firestore connection failed

post.summary: Onboarding endpoint for BUSINESS_OWNER users to create their company profile.
post.description: This endpoint allows new BUSINESS_OWNER users to complete their registration by creating both a Company and User document in Firestore. This endpoint uses lightweight authentication (only verifies Firebase Auth token, does not require User document to exist). This is the first API call a new BUSINESS_OWNER makes after self-registering via Firebase Auth. After this endpoint succeeds, all subsequent API calls will work normally as the user now exists in the User collection.

post.summary: Creates a new physical location for a company.

address.description: The physical address of the location.

post.summary: Pre-registers a user in the system by creating a User document in Firestore.
post.description: This endpoint creates a User document in Firestore to pre-register a user in the system. It does NOT create a Firebase Authentication account - users self-register via Firebase Auth sign-in form. For ATTENDANT role, this pre-registration is required before the user can access API endpoints after authenticating via Firebase. The new user is automatically assigned to the same company as the administrator creating them. This endpoint is designed for administrators to pre-authorize ATTENDANT users or create ADMIN users.

idToken.description: Firebase authentication token of the administrator creating the user. This token is used to verify the admin's identity and extract their company association.

data.description: User data for the new account.

email.description: Email address for the new user. This will be used as their login username and must be unique across all Firebase Authentication users.

firstName.description: First name of the new user.

lastName.description: Last name of the new user.

phoneNumber.description: Phone number of the new user. Optional field for contact purposes.

role.description: Role assignment for the new user. Determines their permissions and access level within the system. BUSINESS_OWNER and ADMIN have full company access, while ATTENDANT has limited permissions.

200.description: User successfully created in both Firebase Authentication and Firestore database.

data.description: The complete User document as stored in Firestore, including all auto-generated fields.

status.description: Status information about the creation operation.

result.description: Indicates a new record was created.

message.description: Human-readable confirmation message with the document ID.

password.description: This field is no longer returned as Firebase Auth accounts are not created by this endpoint. Users self-register via Firebase Auth.

400.description: Bad Request - Invalid input data, missing required fields, duplicate email, or database operation failure.

error.description: Detailed error message explaining what went wrong.
examples: Email is required to create a user.
Role is required to create a user.
Invalid role: INVALID_ROLE. Must be ATTENDANT, BUSINESS_OWNER, or ADMIN.
Failed to save user data: Invalid field value

401.description: Unauthorized - Missing or invalid authentication token.

403.description: Forbidden - Valid token but insufficient permissions or invalid user state.

500.description: Internal Server Error - Unexpected server-side error during user creation.

error.example: Internal Server Error: Firestore connection failed

post.summary: Generates a comprehensive and dynamic set of reports for any specified data model.
post.description: This powerful endpoint provides a one-stop solution for data analysis and visualization. By specifying a model name (e.g., 'Ticket', 'User'), the system introspects the model's schema and automatically generates multiple report variations. This includes a full data dump, a high-level summary, and various permutations that aggregate data based on different fields. It's designed to be the backbone for dashboards, data exports, and business intelligence tasks. The first request for a new model may be slower as the report structures are analyzed and cached; subsequent requests will be significantly faster.

modelName.description: The exact, case-sensitive name of the data model you wish to generate reports for. The model must be defined in the system's schemas.

schema.description: A dynamically generated array of report objects, each tailored to a different analytical perspective. The array always begins with a 'Full Data Report', followed by a 'Summary Report', and then all other calculated permutations.

title.description: The descriptive title of the specific report, indicating its content and perspective.
title.example: Summary Report for Tickets by Status

type.description: The classification of the report, indicating its structure and purpose.

headers.description: An ordered array of strings representing the column headers for the report's data table.

rows.description: An array of data rows. Each row is itself an array of values, ordered to correspond with the 'headers'. All values are returned as strings to ensure type consistency.
